issues.description: Assembly/global relations attach kinetochore_A/B to the chromatid 'center' anchor (i.e., the centromeric constriction point at index 2), but the microtubule constraints 'left_attachment_measured'/'right_attachment_measured' require the microtubule 'end' to coincide with the kinetochore center. The kinetochore centers are at x=±0.285 while the chromatid 'center' anchors are at x=±0.22, so the connect relation target_anchor does not match the actual kinetochore object; the drawn link (pole->kinetochore) and the declared attachment relation (kinetochore->chromatid 'center') use inconsistent endpoints. This is a schematic geometry-vs-identity bookkeeping defect, not a molecular-shape claim, but it can teach wrong attachment points. Repair: make chromatic attachment relation target the 'kinetochore_site' anchor (index 2) and keep kinetochore centers coincident with that site.
issues.repair_scope: relations/anchors only; assets and event ordering preserved
acceptance_criteria: kinetochore_A/B centers coincide with sister_A/B 'kinetochore_site' within tolerance
microtubule ends coincide with kinetochore centers after metaphase
relation target_anchor consistent across assembly and global relations

issues.description: F5 establishes the spindle assembly checkpoint near end of metaphase as a gate before anaphase separation. The event ordering (metaphase->anaphase) is consistent, but no state/transition encodes the checkpoint condition; anaphase split preconditions check 'phase aligned' and bipolar relations, which is an acceptable schematic proxy. Minor: caption/notes could state the checkpoint is assumed passed. If the clip is meant to teach why separation does not start prematurely, this simplification should be explicit.
issues.repair_scope: caption/simplification note or a lightweight checkpoint precondition; do not add new molecular processes
acceptance_criteria: declared simplification or precondition documents that SAC is assumed satisfied before anaphase

issues.description: scientific_simplifications list repeats entries and mixes scope notes; not a science error but reduces auditability. Deduplicate and keep allowed simplifications (one duplicated chromosome; schematic geometry) distinct from omissions.

notes: Facts F1-F8 support the teaching model: two sister chromatids, bipolar attachment, cohesion release, persistent identities as daughter chromosomes. Schematic shapes not treated as molecular evidence.
Deterministic checks report PASS but connection continuity is questionable per anchor mismatch; PASS is withheld until anchor bookkeeping is consistent.
No polarity rule applies (this clip is mitosis metaphase-anaphase, not DNA synthesis strand polarity).
